name: Akvorado
what_it_is: Akvorado is a network flow collection, enrichment, and visualization platform that ingests NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow traffic, enriches flows with SNMP-derived interface names and IPinfo geolocation data, stores them in ClickHouse, and exposes a web UI with timeseries and Sankey diagram views. It was developed and is maintained by Free, a French ISP, and is licensed under AGPLv3.
components: akvorado-inlet: receives raw flow datagrams (NetFlow/IPFIX on UDP 2055 and 4739, sFlow on UDP 6343), decodes and forwards to Kafka
akvorado-orchestrator: central configuration authority that distributes config to other components and manages SNMP polling schedules
akvorado-console: web UI service backed by SQLite (console DB); renders timeseries and Sankey diagrams querying ClickHouse
akvorado-outlet: BGP-based metadata/state exporter (TCP 10179), persists flow state and metadata cache to disk
clickhouse: columnar database storing enriched flow records; accessed by console and outlet
kafka: message bus (KRaft mode, no ZooKeeper) bridging inlet to ClickHouse ingestion pipeline
kafka-ui: browser UI for inspecting Kafka topics and consumer lag
redis: in-memory store used for inter-component coordination/caching
traefik: reverse proxy routing HTTP traffic to orchestrator, console, kafka-ui, and clickhouse with Prometheus metrics endpoint
protocols: SNMP (polling network devices for interface metadata)
BGP (akvorado-outlet exposes TCP 10179 for route/metadata exchange)
measurement: Per-flow byte and packet counters stored in ClickHouse
Interface-level traffic aggregation via SNMP-enriched interface names
Geolocation tagging per source/destination IP using IPinfo.io databases
Timeseries visualization of flow volumes in web console
Sankey diagram visualization of traffic distribution across AS/interface/geo dimensions
Kafka consumer lag observable via kafka-ui
Traefik exposes Prometheus metrics (port 8081) for proxy-level observability
configuration: YAML configuration file mounted into akvorado-orchestrator; distributed at runtime to inlet, console, outlet
Environment variable overrides supported (AKVORADO_CFG_* prefix observed in compose)
Console database DSN set via AKVORADO_CFG_CONSOLE_DATABASE_DSN
Outlet persist paths set via AKVORADO_CFG_OUTLET_METADATA_CACHEPERSISTFILE and AKVORADO_CFG_OUTLET_FLOW_STATEPERSISTFILE
ClickHouse init timeout and user setup controlled via CLICKHOUSE_INIT_TIMEOUT / CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP
Kafka runs in KRaft mode; node ID and roles set via KAFKA_NODE_ID, KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES, KAFKA_LISTENERS
modes: Production/demo: full 9-service docker-compose stack with Traefik ingress and persistent volumes
Public demo instance available at demo.akvorado.net with sample data (read-only)
Grafana plugin integration available for embedding flow data into Grafana dashboards
constraints: No built-in fault injection or traffic replay mechanism — no way to simulate device failures or malformed flow packets from within the stack
Requires external IPinfo.io license/database for geolocation enrichment; without it geo fields are absent
Changelog must be reviewed before every upgrade — the project explicitly warns that schema/config migrations are not automatic
Kafka runs without ZooKeeper (KRaft) but uses a fixed custom bridge subnet (247.16.14.0/24 / fd1c:8ce3:6fb:1::/64), which may conflict with existing network ranges
akvorado-inlet listens only on UDP — flow sources must be configured to send to the inlet's host IP; no TCP flow collection supported
All HTTP services are routed exclusively through Traefik; direct port exposure to the host is limited to Traefik's ports 8080 and 8081

docker_services.name: kafka
docker_services.role: Message bus between inlet and ClickHouse

notable_absences: No NETCONF/YANG or gRPC telemetry ingestion — only UDP-based flow protocols supported
No built-in alerting or threshold-based notifications — purely a collection and visualization tool
No flow replay or pcap import capability for offline analysis
No multi-tenant access control in the open-source version
No native TLS termination on flow receiver ports (inlet uses plain UDP)
